Retry the failures of a bulk Wayback run

Source: R/wayback_save.R
wbrtry.Rd

Picks up where a wbsave run left off: it re-tries only the URLs whose captures failed or were still running, after first checking whether the Wayback Machine already holds a copy of each. Use it after a run that hit archive.org's limits, typically the next day.

Usage

wbrtry(output, incgone = FALSE, lookup = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

output

The JSON Lines results file of an earlier wbsave() run (or of rmbl wayback); results of the retry are appended to it.

incgone

Logical, default FALSE. Also capture again the pages whose failure says the page is gone.

lookup

Logical, default TRUE. Look each failure up in the Wayback Machine (one lookup a second) before capturing again.

...

Passed to wbsave(): jobs, within, the keys, quiet, permin, maxcap.

Value

The whole run as it now stands, one row per URL (a data frame of class rmbl_wayback_save), with the attribute retry: how many failures there were, how many a lookup found, how many were captured again, how many were left as gone, and how many were left for tomorrow (a daily limit hit today), as a one-row data frame with integer columns failed, found_by_lookup, captured_again, left_as_gone and left_for_tomorrow.

Details

Reads the results file a wbsave run wrote and tries again every URL whose latest result is "failed" (or "submitted": a capture a stopped run had started, which is polled rather than submitted again), so nobody has to dig the failures out by hand. Each failed URL is first looked up in the Wayback Machine, one lookup a second: a capture made at any time (an earlier one of a page that has since gone, or one made today by another run when the daily limit refused this one) is recorded as "existing" without capturing again. What is left is captured again with wbsave(), appending to the same file. A page its source no longer has is not sent again unless incgone = TRUE: a new capture would only archive the error. "Gone" means the recorded message contains archive.org's report of the target server's reply ("target server cannot find", "returned 404", "returned 410", "error:not-found" or "error:gone"); an HTTP 404 from archive.org's own API does not count. A failure for a daily limit recorded today (UTC) is not sent again until tomorrow.

Network: the lookups use the Wayback availability API and the new captures use wbsave(), which needs the archive.org keys. When there is nothing left to send, no keys and no network are needed. Each lookup that finds a capture is appended to output as an "existing" line.

Errors: output not a single path to an existing file; incgone or lookup not TRUE or FALSE; any error from wbsave().

See also

wbsave; rmbl wayback --retry FILE.jsonl from the command line.

Examples

# Offline: a results file whose only failure is a page that is gone
# has nothing to send again, so no keys or network are used.
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".jsonl")
writeLines(c(
  paste0('{"url":"https://example.org/","status":"saved",',
         '"timestamp":"20260101120000",',
         '"snapshot":"https://web.archive.org/web/20260101120000/https://example.org/",',
         '"message":"","at":"2026-01-01T12:00:00Z"}'),
  paste0('{"url":"https://example.org/old","status":"failed",',
         '"message":"target server cannot find the page","at":"2026-01-01T12:00:00Z"}')
), f)
res <- wbrtry(f, lookup = FALSE)
res
#> ── Wayback Machine captures ────────────────────────────────────── 
#>   2 URLs: 1 saved, 0 existing, 1 failed
#> 
#>  status      timestamp                     url
#>   saved 20260101120000    https://example.org/
#>  failed           <NA> https://example.org/old
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 
attr(res, "retry")
#>   failed found_by_lookup captured_again left_as_gone left_for_tomorrow
#> 1      1               0              0            1                 0

try(wbrtry(tempfile(fileext = ".jsonl")))
#> Error : no results file at /tmp/RtmpvHPAuK/file1e9618fb9cd9.jsonl

# With failures to resend, keys and the network are needed.
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- wbsave(urls, output = "snapshots.jsonl")
# later, or the next day once the daily capture limits have reset:
res <- wbrtry("snapshots.jsonl")
attr(res, "retry")
} # }
